title: LST with a heralded filter: streamed shift testing, tolerance 1-1/(10^64-3)^4

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s modulo N, n=ceil(log2 N), LST in proof.md uses k=n+4 tests per candidate, a global cap 48N on handed-over copies, and the specified streamed linear-size reversible arithmetic; every acquisition goes through the heralded filter FILTER of proof.md's final section (the identity in the clean problem, literal raw-acquisition cutoff 48 D N with D = (10^64-3)^4 under the heralded model). It recovers the entire s with unconditional probability >5/6. On every branch its total charged work is O(N n log2(n+2)), hence the uniform envelope B_T(n)=2^n n log2 n for n>=2; its exact growth index is 1. All constants are absolute; all four resource bounds hold jointly for this single configuration on every branch, in the clean problem and under the heralded malformed-copy model of claim 4 (proof.md Theorem H.3), jointly with the tolerance of claim 4.

It recovers the entire s with unconditional probability >5/6. On every branch the number of acquired source copies is at most 48N in the clean problem and at most 48 D N raw copies under the heralded model (proof.md Lemma H.1 and Theorem H.3; D is a fixed absolute integer), including failures, discarded and reset copies; hence O(N) = O(2^n) in both cases, and its uniform envelope B_samples(n)=2^n has exact growth index 1. All constants are absolute; all four resource bounds hold jointly for this single configuration on every branch, in the clean problem and under the heralded malformed-copy model of claim 4 (proof.md Theorem H.3), jointly with the tolerance of claim 4.

For every N>=2 and s modulo N, n=ceil(log2 N), LST with the heralded filter FILTER of proof.md's final section (k=n+4 tests per candidate, cap 48N on handed-over copies, literal raw-acquisition cutoff 48 D N, D = x^4, x = 10^64 - 3) proves fractional error tolerance epsilon(n) = 9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999996*9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999998*5909009547859618446014307935656485996455360061473289284034355157*8461654968574415353741992088106541809421651544931744139485636465*2/9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999997^4 = 1 - 1/x^4, a constant in (0,1), under the heralded malformed-copy model stated in the structured error_model; the displayed integers of proof.md's final section multiply to x^2 + 1. If at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed on every branch, the algorithm recovers the entire s with unconditional probability >5/6 jointly with the four resource bounds of claims 0-3 in the form stated there (proof.md Lemmas H.1-H.2, Theorem H.3). In the clean problem (no herald) the algorithm is exactly LST. No tolerance of undetectable corruption is claimed.

structured.error_model: Heralded malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires on an execution branch, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Each acquired copy consists of an (n+1)-qubit register of the ideal copy's shape together with one classical herald bit f delivered with it. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed. A well-formed copy has f = 0 and its register is a fresh copy of rho_s, in tensor product with every other system (earlier copies, the adversary's system and the algorithm's registers). A malformed copy has f = 1 and its register is in an arbitrary state chosen by the adversary, possibly entangled with the adversary's private system and with other malformed copies. On every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. The herald is always correct, so malformation is detectable (an erasure-type error); its timing, its number within the promise and the malformed register contents are adversarial. In the clean problem no herald is supplied and every copy is well-formed. No source control, purification access or preparation inverse is supplied.
